body: The cleanup interval dropped from 10 minutes to 1 minute. That looks like a debugging leftover. Every cleanup job (annotations, snapshots, dashboard versions, tmp files, etc.) would now run 10x more often, which adds DB load and extra contention with annotation inserts, the very thing this PR is trying to reduce. It isn't mentioned in the PR description, so please revert to `time.Minute * 10`.

These look like debug logs left in. They log at **Error** level on every batch, including the success path and the final empty batch, so every cleanup cycle floods logs and alerting with false errors. They also dump the full `ids` slice, which can be tens of thousands of IDs per line with large batch sizes. Please remove them, or downgrade to Debug and log counts only. The same applies to lines 537, 554, 557, 576 and 579.

Building the IN list by repeatedly calling `fmt.Sprintf("%s, %d", values, v)` is O(n²): each iteration copies the whole string again. With the batch sizes this branch exists for (e.g. 32767 in the new test), that's hundreds of MB of allocation and copying per batch. Use `strings.Builder`, or `strconv.FormatInt` plus `strings.Join`.

The parameter-limit handling only covers SQLite. MySQL and Postgres both cap prepared-statement placeholders at 65535, so an `AnnotationCleanupJobBatchSize` above that makes every DELETE fail on those databases. Before this PR the cleanup was a single subquery statement and had no such limit, so this is a regression for large configured batch sizes. Consider chunking `ids` into sub-batches of at most N parameters instead of special-casing SQLite by the configured batch size. Also, the comment says the limit is 999, but that only holds for SQLite < 3.32.0; newer versions allow 32766.

The SELECT and the DELETE now run in separate sessions, so the loop's termination condition has changed. `untilDoneOrCancelled` stops as soon as a batch reports 0 affected rows. If another Grafana instance (HA setup) or a user deletes the fetched IDs between `fetchIDs` and `deleteByIDs`, the DELETE affects 0 rows and cleanup stops early even though more matching rows remain. Consider ending the loop on `len(ids) == 0` instead of `affected == 0`.
